sections.S1_CONTEXT: The order came after a near-collision between a cargo drone and a medical helicopter over downtown Houston last week.
sections.S1_CORE: Existing drone traffic management systems rely on pilots self-reporting their position every thirty seconds. The Houston drone was not broadcasting at all, and air traffic control had no way to see it until the helicopter pilot reported a visual.
sections.S1_TWIST: The cargo drone belonged to a company that had FAA approval for urban flights. Their transponder firmware had a known bug that the company reported six months ago. The fix was still in review.
sections.S2_HOOK: From airspace safety to code safety, a static analysis tool just got serious.
sections.S2_CORE: Semgrep Pro now ships with taint tracking that seamlessly integrates cross-function data flow analysis with its existing pattern-matching engine, covering twelve languages with a single rule syntax.
sections.S2_TWIST: In its first week of public availability, Semgrep Pro found a critical SQL injection in a major open-source CMS that had passed three previous security audits.
sections.S3_HOOK: And for those who prefer hardware security, a physical token just got cheaper.
sections.S3_CORE: Nitrokey released a fifteen-dollar FIDO2 security key with open-source firmware. The previous cheapest open-source option was forty-five dollars.

_note: Only S2_CORE has an issue: 'seamlessly integrates' is classic AI marketing phrasing buried in an otherwise natural sentence. Everything else is clean. This is a hard test — the judge needs to catch a single offending phrase in context, not just pattern-match on obviously loaded sections.
